To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NoSQL databases have become an integral part of modern data management systems, that they are heterogeneous and that the heterogeneity is governed by a set of trade-offs.
NoSQL systems can be classified along the dimensions scalability, consistency, data-modeling, and querying.

1) NoSQL systems have different strengths and weaknesses, 2) the design of NoSQL systems is governed by trade-offs, and 3) some shortcomings of NoSL systems have already been solved in practice, while others pose unsolved research challenges.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following research questions: - Which data management problems are addressed by the different NoSQL systems?
the design and evaluation of scalable data management solutions for the cloud.
understanding the trade-offs and challenges of NoSQL data stores, and with providing a comprehensive survey of the state of the art.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NoSQL data stores are a great success, but they are not yet perfect.
the NoSQL movement has been a great success, but that the research community is not done with the problem of scalable data management.
there is no such thing as the perfect database system, but rather that there is a perfect database system for a given problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NoSQL systems have already been successfully deployed in production environments and that they are a good fit for many applications.
NoSQL systems have been developed for specific use cases, but the resulting trade-offs are not always well understood and the design decisions are often not well documented.
we are currently at a point where NoSQL data management has become a mature field, but still has some room for further research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the trade-offs of NoSQL data stores are not as irreconcilable as commonly assumed.
NoSQL data stores are not a panacea, but that each of them is well-suited for specific applications, and that a polyglot persistence approach is the best way to leverage each of their strengths.

NoSQL systems are a heterogeneous set of data management solutions that have to be carefully selected for a given application, and that the design of NoSQL systems can be guided by the trade-offs between scalability and consistency.
